## Problem

- The on-call rotation can get a false `IngestionAnalyticsSinglePartitionDelayed` page for a partition that is not behind.
- A pod keeps exporting `latest_processed_timestamp_ms` for partitions it gave up in a rebalance.
- That stale value ages. The alert takes `max by (groupId, topic, partition)`, so the stale value wins while the new owner has no series for the partition, for example an idle partition.

## Changes

- `IngestionConsumer` removes the gauge series of each revoked partition, so only the current owner reports a partition.
- `KafkaConsumerInterface.connect` takes the optional `onPartitionsRevoked` hook that `KafkaConsumerV2` already supports. The analytics lanes run v2 (`CONSUMER_USE_V2`).
- `KafkaConsumer` (v1) also calls the hook, after it unassigns the partitions, without waiting for it. v2 awaits it before unassigning.
- Stacked on #105238. That PR removes v1's `false` rebalance mode, in which node-rdkafka rebalanced on its own and v1 never saw the revoke.

> [!NOTE]
> A partition whose new owner stalls before it processes any message now has no series, so this alert does not fire for it. A pod restart already has the same effect. The all-partitions and stopped-consuming alerts still cover a stalled lane.

## How did you test this code?

- Extended the v1 revoke test in `consumer-v1.test.ts`: it fails if v1 stops calling the hook. Ran locally.
- Added `should stop exporting the processed timestamp of revoked partitions` to `ingestion-consumer.serial.test.ts`: it fails if the revoked partition keeps its series or a retained partition loses its series.
- Not run: the serial ingestion consumer suite, because no local Postgres was available. CI runs it.
